key_insight: Fault-tolerant spin-qubit quantum computers may become energetically competitive before they become faster than classical computers, with energy crossover occurring at smaller problem sizes than runtime crossover.
engineering_relevance: The work identifies cryogenic cooling, instrumentation, and decoding as the main system-level energy bottlenecks, and shows that control-signal demultiplexing can cut energy use by about two orders of magnitude.
method: Built a detailed power/energy budget for a Loss-DiVincenzo silicon spin-qubit computer.
Compared the Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT) against the classical FFT under polynomially bounded sampling assumptions.
Extended the analysis to surface-code QEC, including QEC cycles, gate synthesis, and decoding costs.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports an estimated ~100 kW power draw for a system with about one million physical qubits, and benchmarks energetic crossover against FFT-based classical computation.
watch_item: The 100 kW estimate depends on hardware assumptions such as cryogenic overhead, demultiplexing ratio, and decoding efficiency, so real systems could vary substantially.
paper_title: Energetics of Fault-Tolerant Spin-Qubit Quantum Computation
